subject.name: Registered Agent Commerce Pattern
subject.scope_statement: Generalized agent-registration and delegated-accountability pattern in agentic commerce and payment settings.

normative_governance.description: Delegated authority and dispute accountability are only partially specified.

measurement_substrate.description: Traceability and registration claims are visible, but dispute-grade accountability mechanics remain underspecified.

deliberative_layer.description: Trust and registration language is prominent in the public framing.

governance_shape.name: Delegated Agent Accountability
governance_shape.summary: Technical registration must be joined to accountable principal binding, scope, revocation, and dispute traceability.
validated_assumptions: Registered or tokenized agent identity is not equivalent to legal personhood.
Traceability must reach a responsible principal.

approved_conditions: agent acts only within explicit delegated scope
departure_signals: traceability stops at technical agent identity
intervention_rules: do not treat registration alone as sufficient accountability

lifecycle_validation.notes: Illustrative case pattern, not a live deployed system profile.

risk_profile.summary: Primary risk is accountability displacement rather than host compromise.

authority.notes: Agent may initiate consequential transactions under delegated authority.

reach.notes: Dependent on connected merchant, wallet, or payment scope.

reversibility.notes: Some transactions may be disputed or reversed, but not without cost.

coupling.notes: Coupling grows where agent identity, registration, and payment rails combine.

consequence.notes: Consequences include financial loss, dispute complexity, and accountability confusion.

composition.notes: Risk increases when registration, authentication, and transaction authority are treated as one solved problem.

failure_classes.notes: The central risk is accountability displacement.
Risk profile questions often remain weaker than the trust language.

anti_patterns.summary: Framework or trust claims outpace explicit risk profiling.

tests.notes: Pattern-level materials do not reliably expose a full deployment-specific risk profile.

anti_patterns.summary: Technical agent identity risks being mistaken for accountable legal standing.

tests.notes: Delegation chain details are not fully visible in the generalized public pattern.
Trust and registration language can overstate what technical identity proves.

evidence_summary.description: Public agentic-commerce materials emphasize registration, trust, and traceability.
Generalized pattern analysis in the repository's registered-agent accountability case study.

residual_risk: Registration can still mask weak delegation accountability.

demotion_backlog.title: Bind agent credentials to accountable delegated principals
